docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Boti's architecture is well-positioned for PyArrow integration. The ManagedResource lifecycle, DataGateway abstraction, and existing PyArrow filesystem usage provide a clean foundation. By introducing Arrow as a first-class in-memory representation — starting with SQL partition loading and schema coercion — Boti can achieve significant performance gains without breaking changes or new dependencies.

The phased approach ensures: 1. Immediate value (Phase 1: 2–5x SQL load speedup) 2. Low risk (opt-in, backward compatible) 3. Progressive enhancement (each phase builds on the last) 4. No new dependencies (uses existing pyarrow)

Next step: Implement Phase 1 with a feature flag, benchmark against production workloads, and validate performance gains before proceeding.

docs.title: Security Hardening Guide
docs.text: This guide documents defensive defaults and validation hooks for SQL and Datacube paths in boti-data.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• SQL reads through DataGateway and DataHelper
  • Datacube request validation via DatacubeContract
  • Distributed SQL worker credential handling

docs.title: Filter Interpolation Hotspots
docs.text:
Use this matrix during reviews to identify where dynamic filter/query inputs are accepted and what control should be enforced.

Module Entry point Risk type Recommended control src/boti_data/gateway/normalization.py split_control_and_filters(), normalize_configured_filters() Runtime kwargs not in LOAD_CONTROL_KEYS are treated as filters and merged with sticky/explicit filters. Restrict caller-provided kwargs shape and validate allowed filter keys at API boundary. src/boti_data/gateway/core.py _build_configured_request() Merged semantic filters are forwarded into SQL query construction. Enforce semantic field allowlists and keep field_map translation enabled where DB names differ. src/boti_data/field_map.py translate_filters_to_db() Dynamic filter keys are rewritten into DB-column keys, including nested boolean operators. Validate semantic keys before translation; reject unknown/suspicious operator forms. src/boti_data/filters/handler.py compile_filters(), apply_filters() Dynamic field__op expressions compile into backend-specific conditions. Keep operator parsing strict and test forbidden keys/ops in security regressions. src/boti_data/gateway/loaders.py _prepare_sql_statement() Raw sql text is accepted when allowed; app-side string interpolation can bypass intent. Prefer raw_sql_policy="disabled" for production and require bound params for any approved raw SQL. src/boti_data/parquet/reader.py _normalize_filter_options() Bare kwargs are promoted into filters, which may broaden query scope unexpectedly. Use explicit filters= in higher-risk call paths and lint/review wildcard runtime kwargs. src/boti_data/datacube/resource.py _prepare_request() Datacube filters/cube names are accepted unless contract validator is configured. Make DatacubeContract.request_validator mandatory in production configs.

docs.title: Raw SQL Is Denied by Default
docs.text: sql= execution requires an explicit allow_raw_sql=True opt-in. Without that flag, loads fail fast.

docs.title: Raw SQL Is Read-Only Only
docs.text: Even when enabled, only single-statement read-only SELECT/WITH queries are accepted. Mutating or multi-statement payloads are rejected.

docs.title: Disable Raw SQL Entirely
docs.text: For stricter deployments, initialize DataGateway(..., raw_sql_policy="disabled"). This blocks all sql= calls, including those with allow_raw_sql=True.

docs.title: Always Bind Parameters
docs.text:
Use bound parameters instead of string interpolation:

frame = gateway.load(
    sql="SELECT id, status FROM users WHERE status = :status",
    params={"status": status_value},
    as_pandas=True,
    allow_raw_sql=True,
)

Do not build SQL with f-strings or concatenated user input.

docs.title: Datacube Hardening
docs.text:
Datacube security policy is contract-driven. If no request_validator is configured, suspicious cubes/filter keys can be accepted by permissive loaders.

Use a strict validator to enforce business and security constraints:

def request_validator(request):
    cube_name = str(request.cube or "")
    if ".." in cube_name or "/" in cube_name:
        raise ValueError("cube name contains forbidden path tokens")
    if any(str(key).startswith("$") for key in request.filters):
        raise ValueError("operator-style filter keys are not allowed")

Attach it with DatacubeContract(request_validator=...).

You can enforce validator presence at gateway construction time:

gateway = DataGateway(
    DatacubeConfig(loader=loader, contract=contract),
    require_datacube_request_validator=True,
)

docs.title: Strict Filter Validation (Opt-In)
docs.text:
DataGateway supports optional strict controls for configured-mode and datacube filter payloads:

  • strict_filter_validation=True
  • allowed_filter_fields={...}
  • max_filter_depth=...
  • max_filter_conditions=...
  • max_in_filter_values=...

Example:

gateway = DataGateway(
    sql_config,
    table="users",
    strict_filter_validation=True,
    allowed_filter_fields={"status", "created_at"},
    max_filter_depth=6,
    max_filter_conditions=64,
    max_in_filter_values=1000,
)

docs.title: Distributed SQL Credential Handling
docs.text:
For distributed execution, set worker_connection_env_var on SqlDatabaseConfig so task payloads do not serialize raw DSNs:

config = SqlDatabaseConfig(
    connection_url="postgresql+psycopg://...",
    worker_connection_env_var="DB_DSN",
)

Ensure the configured env var is present on every worker.
